name: The Merrion
insider_take: Dublin's most elegant Georgian sanctuary, where Irish hospitality meets aristocratic grandeur in the heart of the capital.
whats_special: The Merrion occupies four meticulously restored Georgian townhouses dating from the 1760s, featuring Ireland's largest private art collection with over 100 original pieces. The hotel's gardens are the only hotel gardens in Dublin city center, originally laid out in 1750 and still maintained in period style.
pro_tip: Book afternoon tea in The Upper Lounge - it's served on Shelley bone china while overlooking the historic gardens, and you might spot government ministers from nearby Leinster House (Ireland's Parliament) just next door.
dont_miss: The hotel's two-Michelin-starred Restaurant Patrick Guilbaud, Ireland's only two-star establishment, and a stroll through the adjacent Government Gardens. Trinity College and the Book of Kells are just a 3-minute walk away.
pros: Prime location in Dublin's city center near Trinity College and shopping districts
Historic Georgian elegance with luxurious modern amenities and world-class spa
Exceptional dining options including Michelin-starred Restaurant Patrick Guilbaud
Impeccable service and attention to detail with personalized guest experiences
cons: Historic building may have smaller room sizes in some categories
